question: Does a one-sided fallback -- default to BoD, serve base only when BoD's OWN absolute coherence is below tau -- beat always-BoD at a low intervention rate, where the symmetric 'pick the more coherent model' rules failed?

config.policy: serve base iff bod_coherence < tau, else serve BoD
config.trigger_definition: mean off-diagonal cosine among the top-10 result vectors (same encoder that retrieved them)
config.population: all 250 holdout queries (the real serving population)
config.api_note: $0 -- pure numpy re-analysis of cached features and labels

always_bod.rule: reference -- serve BoD on every query

symmetric_pick_higher_coherence.rule: serve whichever model has the higher coherence (zdiff_coherence > 0)

zdiff_coherence_threshold_in_sample.rule: serve base when zdiff_coherence < -1.488 (in-sample optimum, junk objective)
zdiff_coherence_threshold_in_sample.verdict: non-significant wash, and this is the in-sample optimum

oracle_categorical.rule: ORACLE -- serve the per-query categorical winner

oracle_click.rule: ORACLE -- serve the per-query click winner

combined.note: OPTIMISTIC UPPER BOUND -- but no tau beat always-BoD even with the threshold fitted on the same queries it is scored on
